VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

1. [blocker] hub/src/crew_health/platform/storage.py:58: Application SQL can commit outside the unit of work.

   Evidence: SQLiteSession rejects transaction words only when they are the first whitespace-delimited token. The write authorizer at line 144 does not deny SQLITE_TRANSACTION or SQLITE_SAVEPOINT. A review probe inserted a row, executed `/* application SQL */ COMMIT`, then raised before the enclosing command could finish. The row remained after rollback, without the command receipt or audit. This violates SYSTEM 5.6 and AGENTS rules 6 and shared transaction ownership.

   Required change: Enforce transaction and savepoint ownership at the SQLite authorization boundary, with a narrowly scoped internal path for the unit of work. Reject application BEGIN, COMMIT, END, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT and RELEASE regardless of comments or whitespace. Add failing-first regressions that verify state, ledger, audit, events and replication all roll back together after attempted escape and after a later failure.

2. [blocker] hub/src/crew_health/platform/application/private.py:301: A conflicting deletion command destroys a key before idempotency rejects it.

   Evidence: delete checks only platform_private_deletion at line 323, calls vault.revoke at line 335, and consults the permanent command ledger only at line 384. Reusing an already accepted private-entry command key for deleteJournal returned DUPLICATE_COMMAND in the review probe after the vault reported the entry revoked. The hub still had deleted=0 and deletion completed=0. Recovery then raised INTERNAL_ERROR. An invalid command must not destroy an accepted record.

   Required change: Reserve and validate the full shared command identity against the durable ledger and intent mechanism before any vault side effect, including collisions with every other operation and target. Recheck authorization at the appropriate phases, preserve the original receipt, and make each valid deletion phase durable and idempotent. Test same key with another operation, resource, owner and body, including concurrent retries; every conflict must leave keys and records untouched.

3. [blocker] hub/src/crew_health/platform/application/private.py:245: Private recovery cannot finish interrupted deletion.

   Evidence: recover processes only the first page of pending sealed entries and then verifies live references. It never reads platform_private_deletion or resumes vault revocation and tombstoning. A crash after successful revoke but before the hub tombstone leaves an undecryptable reference classified as live. The deletion-collision probe also exercised this stranded state. backup_barrier at line 294 likewise performs only one pending page. SYSTEM 5.8.1 and 7.4 require interrupted deletions to resume without resurrecting keys.

   Required change: Recover persisted deletion intents against the current vault before live-reference verification and before serving or backup. Resume incomplete replica acknowledgements and tombstones, handle pending seals for deleted entries, and drain bounded pages under an overall bound rather than examining only the first page. Inject process loss before and after each deletion phase, an offline vault replica, multiple recovery pages, and restore of a pre-deletion backup. Assert one receipt, visible pending status, no resurrection, and unrelated entries still decrypt.

Use existing owned assembly/generation paths; obtain an allocation through the coordinator if a new generated leaf is required. Add a real added-module startup test proving its migration, provider, route and hooks execute without editing assembly, plus tampered, missing and unexpected module rejection.

Preserve the freeze until correction and sweep are durable. Test startup, forward and backward jumps after startup, restart, delayed observations, relative timers, absolute deadlines and mission-day boundaries through the assembled runtime. Do not substitute a fake clock or force the frozen flag off.

Stream backup hashing with a bounded buffer and cancellation/deadline checks. Release admission/writer locks and close partial connections on every failure, including connection and target creation failure. Persist the specified opaque-origin-token/projection-hash deduplication alongside contiguous delivery checkpoints and reconcile it on restore without exposing raw origin sequence. Test two senders to one recipient, a restored sender, replay across streams, same token with changed projection, lost acknowledgements and crash at each apply/checkpoint boundary.

Failure detail and rerun interpretation:

- ticket.T5.1 failed only on the Hypothesis timing instability described in finding 21; its exact rerun passed 18 tests. No assertion or deadline was changed.
- ticket.T6.2 reports 18 errors and 37 warnings from the known shared-document lint defect. The E01 design itself passes all 15 checks without warnings.
- ticket.T6.9 initially found one stale TypeScript module manifest during concurrent module work. The mandatory generator runs refreshed it under D26; the exact rerun passes both interfaces and generated validators, with 132 interface details and 214 generated-artifact details. No guard was bypassed.
- Corpus reported 82 errors initially and 78 in the later ticket invocation. Both runs failed. The later output contains 611 explicitly passing details; other details report which checks executed. Missing real contributors and runtime documents remain failures.
- ticket.T6.11 initially stopped during collection because the concurrently added eval/scenarios/conftest.py imported unavailable crew_health_harness. The later exact rerun passed 313 tests with 23 ResourceWarnings, after the shared workspace changed. No PYTHONPATH workaround, fixture override or collection exclusion was applied. The initial dependent coverage validator had no report; the later validator measured 52 executable files and failed 29.
- Trace lacks T-E01-10 and T-E01-19. Safety reports private.delete complexity 19, above 15, and missing true/false execution evidence for 755 conditions. Mutation validation reports missing execution evidence for 761 mutants. A passing pytest process does not supply these absent artifacts.
- Generation emits the documented AwareDatetime/pattern warning and TypeScript duplicate-example-name warnings. The installed Instant validator was checked through generation and its tests; these warnings are not suppressed. The full-hub warning is a Starlette/httpx deprecation. Coverage runs exposed unclosed SQLite connections, addressed by finding 8.

Review scope, accepted corrections and limitations

Read AGENTS.md, E01 design and PLAN, task/ticket briefs and owned code/tests, SYSTEM mechanisms and seams used by the design, coordinator decisions, T1.report.md, T1.gates.log, T2.report.md, T2.gates and plan-review-r1.md. There were no earlier build review-r*.md files, blocked notes or violations notes in docs/build/E01 at review start. The design exists, so the missing-design fallback does not apply.

Accepted with evidence: D19 base SHA inventory and disabled external intake until E20 supplies signatures; the verified additive overlay path and rejection tests; manifest-owned generated output placement; the Instant pattern postprocessor restoring a source constraint; exactly the SYSTEM-mandated module-to-registry/API-to-error composition edges; explicit kernel enum re-exports. These follow the current shared rules and passed their respective generation/interface tests. The overlay is partial D12 work, not completed unit-mapping delivery. D25 and D26 are already decided and must not be treated as pending. Safe unavailable behavior for missing signatures/CLI providers does not waive an acceptance criterion.

The interface validator matched 132 declarations, strict type checks passed, and discovered import contracts passed. No additional unresolved handwritten name or justified speculative feature was found beyond the incomplete/duplicate orchestration mechanisms identified above. Current concrete E01 files map to the task allocation. Historical out-of-scope edits cannot be proven absent from the current tree alone: no pre-coder baseline was supplied and git use was prohibited. This review does not certify that history.

The workspace changed during review as other epics added modules and configuration. Import-contract counts grew from 37 to 111 and then 133. Baseline hashing found no changed handwritten E01 source among the files captured at review start. The mandated generation commands refreshed the two generated manifests; other authors changed identity, consent and knowledge files. Findings use the inspected E01 source, and transient integration failures and their exact reruns are retained above. The reviewer made no manual product-code or test edits and ran no git commands.

Additional direct probes used temporary SQLite databases and the existing test fixtures: comment-prefixed COMMIT escaped rollback; deletion with a reused command key revoked the vault before conflict; two source nodes produced the same replica stream; withdrawn authorization prevented revocation; a caller-defined /journal projection passed validation; interleaved source readings defeated stuck detection; the actual installed module tree failed core catalog verification; and degraded component state still yielded Health.status=ok. These are defect reproductions, not counted as passing acceptance tests. Finding descriptions give the inputs and outcomes for the required failing-first regressions.

Installed-artifact probe: built a temporary copy with `uv build /tmp/e01-review-r1/package --wheel --out-dir /tmp/e01-review-r1/dist`, exported locked runtime requirements using `uv export --project hub --no-dev --no-emit-project --format requirements-txt --output-file /tmp/e01-review-r1/runtime-requirements.txt`, and installed that wheel and those requirements in an isolated environment. `/tmp/e01-review-r1/runtime/bin/python -c 'import crew_health.app.assembly'` failed with ModuleNotFoundError for yaml. Wheel inspection found zero SQL migrations and only the generated manifest as JSON package data. No dependency or package source was modified for this probe.
